test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: 18 boys and 24 girls can complete a piece of work in 16 days. All of them started working together but after 12 working days, all girls and 6 boys stopped working. 12 boys completed the remaining work in 9 days. How many days will it take to complete the entire job if only 24 girls have to complete the job?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done in 12 days by **18B + 24G** = 12/16 = 3/4 of the total work.

Remaining work = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4 of total work.

**12 boys** take 9 days for 1/4 work → 12 boys take 36 days for full work → **1 boy efficiency** = 1/(12 × 36) = 1/432.

Total work from initial condition: 16 × (18/432 + 24G) = 1 → 18/432 + 24G = 1/16 → 1/24 + 24G = 1/16 → 24G = 1/16 − 1/24 = 1/48.

**24 girls** efficiency = 1/48 per day → Time taken = 48 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 18 Boys (B) and 24 Girls (G) work for 16 days. After 12 days, 12 Boys complete the rest in 9 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Total Work (W) = 16 × (18B + 24G)

⇒ Work done in 12 days = 12 × (18B + 24G)

⇒ Remaining work = (16 − 12) × (18B + 24G) = 4 × (18B + 24G)

⇒ Remaining work is completed by 12 boys in 9 days = 12B × 9 = 108B

⇒ 4 × (18B + 24G) = 108B

⇒ 72B + 96G = 108B

⇒ 96G = 36B → 8G = 3B → 1B = (8/3)G

⇒ Total Work = 16 × [18 × (8/3)G + 24G] = 16 × [48G + 24G] = 16 × 72G

⇒ Time for 24 girls = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of 24 girls

⇒ Time = (16 × 72G) ÷ 24G = 16 × 3 = 48 days

**∴ The correct answer is 48 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Concept

Total work is often expressed as the product of the number of workers and the days taken: W = M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂.

Efficiency Ratio

If efficiencies are given as E₁ and E₂, then Work = (n₁E₁ + n₂E₂) × Days. This allows conversion between different worker types (e.g., boys to girls).

Remaining Work Rule

When workers leave, focus on the remaining portion of work: (Remaining Days × Original Team) = (New Days × New Team).</p
